title: Arbitration clause drafting mistakes that cause disputes later
p1:
A single sentence in a contract can decide whether a dispute is resolved smoothly or becomes a long legal battle.

Many businesses focus on signing the agreement but overlook the arbitration clause hidden inside it.
p2:
A common misconception is that simply writing “all disputes will be settled by arbitration” is enough.

But vague clauses often create new disputes about the arbitration itself — like who will appoint the arbitrator, where the proceedings will happen, or which rules will apply.
p3:
A well-drafted arbitration clause should remove uncertainty before a conflict begins. It should clearly mention key details such as the arbitration process, governing rules, location, and appointment method.

The surprising part? Parties sometimes spend months arguing over how to start arbitration because the clause meant to avoid disputes was poorly drafted.

A few careful words at the contract stage can save years of time, money, and stress later.
